standard_prerequisites.name: Relative pseudo-coherence of a complex is preserved by localizing the algebra at an element, which gives one of the two implications
standard_prerequisites.use: Disposes of the implication from the second to the first condition.

standard_prerequisites.name: The algebra can be presented by a polynomial ring in the elements and their complementary coefficients modulo the relation expressing that the elements generate the unit ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the polynomial presentation to which the transfers of relative pseudo-coherence are applied.

standard_prerequisites.name: The quotient presenting the algebra is pseudo-coherent as a module over the polynomial ring and remains so after inverting one of the elements, and relative pseudo-coherence transfers to a larger algebra under this hypothesis
standard_prerequisites.use: Moves the hypothesis from the localized algebras to the polynomial ring and back, giving the other implication.

core_obligations: Dispose of the implication that relative pseudo-coherence implies its localizations using the localization statement (proof lines 21683-21685).

For the converse, write the partition of unity as a finite sum and present the algebra by a polynomial ring in the elements, their complementary coefficients and further variables, modulo the relation expressing the sum as one (proof lines 21686-21695).
Record that this quotient is pseudo-coherent as a module over the polynomial ring and that it remains so after inverting one of the elements (proof lines 21695-21699).

Use the transfer of relative pseudo-coherence to conclude that each localized complex is m-pseudo-coherent over the localized polynomial ring, then apply the glueing statement for pseudo-coherence and the transfer of the hypothesis to obtain that the complex is pseudo-coherent over the polynomial ring, which gives the conclusion (proof lines 21699-21711).
proof_roadmap: Present the algebra with the relation expressing the partition of unity and record the pseudo-coherence of the presentation (proof lines 21686-21699).
Transfer relative pseudo-coherence in both directions and glue along the chosen elements (proof lines 21699-21711).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a finite type map and elements generating the unit ideal of the algebra, relative pseudo-coherence of a complex is equivalent to relative pseudo-coherence of each of its localizations at those elements, and the same for pseudo-coherence (statement lines 21668-21681). One implication is the localization statement, while the converse requires presenting the algebra by a polynomial ring in the elements and their complementary coefficients modulo the relation expressing the partition of unity, checking that this presentation is pseudo-coherent over the polynomial ring, and then transferring relative pseudo-coherence from the localized algebras up to the polynomial ring and back, using the glueing statement along the way (proof lines 21683-21711). The presentation and the two transfers are what turn a local hypothesis into a global conclusion. The counted span refers three times to earlier results of this chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
